entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antipater of Bostra was a Greek prelate who served as Metropolitan bishop of Bostra in the Roman province of Arabia during the 5th century AD. He was a foremost critic of Origen and played a significant role in the development of early Christian theology. Antipater's writings had a lasting impact on the formation of the Christian canon and influenced the development of Eastern Orthodoxy.

Born in 400 CE, Antipater rose to prominence in the 440s CE, becoming a key figure in the debates surrounding Origen's teachings. He was ultimately excommunicated by Emperor Theodosius I in 450 CE for his opposition to Origen's views.

As a result of his efforts, Antipater of Bostra left a lasting legacy in the realm of Christian theology, contributing to the shaping of the Christian canon and influencing the development of Eastern Orthodoxy. His work continues to be studied by scholars today, providing valuable insights into the intellectual and theological debates of the 5th century AD.

One notable example of Antipater's influence can be seen in the work of Pope Gelasius I, who built upon Antipater's teachings in his own writings on the nature of the Trinity.
